additional_findings.explanation: The quickstart writing snippet uses unqualified `datetime(...)` and `utc` names that are not imported or defined in the shown snippet; tomlkit's own exported `datetime` takes an RFC 3339 string, so the example as written does not run as-is.

doc_citation.quote:
>>> from tomlkit import comment
>>> from tomlkit import document
>>> from tomlkit import nl
>>> from tomlkit import table

>>> doc = document()
>>> doc.add(comment("This is a TOML document."))
>>> doc.add(nl())
>>> doc.add("title", "TOML Example")
>>> # Using doc["title"] = "TOML Example" is also possible

>>> owner = table()
>>> owner.add("name", "Tom Preston-Werner")
>>> owner.add("organization", "GitHub")
>>> owner.add("bio", "GitHub Cofounder & CEO\nLikes tater tots and beer.")
>>> owner.add("dob", datetime(1979, 5, 27, 7, 32, tzinfo=utc))
>>> owner["dob"].comment("First class dates? Why not?")

additional_findings.proposed_fix: Add the missing standard-library imports (`from datetime import datetime, timezone`, then `utc = timezone.utc`) before the writing example, or replace the line with `owner.add("dob", tomlkit.datetime("1979-05-27T07:32:00Z"))`.

repros.error_excerpt: AssertionError: docs claim 1.0.0 compliance but tomlkit accepts TOML 1.1.0-only inline-table syntax
repros.argument_finding_is_false: A newer parser can remain backward-compatible with the older specification, so supporting 1.1.0 does not technically invalidate a 1.0.0-compliance statement.
repros.script:
import tomlkit

text = "foo = {\n  bar = 1,\n}\n"

parsed = tomlkit.parse(text)  # DOC-LITERAL
assert False, "docs claim 1.0.0 compliance but tomlkit accepts TOML 1.1.0-only inline-table syntax"  # DOC-LITERAL
print("DOCS_OK")

repros.argument_finding_is_false: The cited block could theoretically be run in a doctest namespace where standard-library names were already imported by an earlier example, and tomlkit itself exports a datetime function with the same name that could shadow a stdlib import; however, the shown block begins with its own explicit imports and defines neither datetime nor utc, so as a standalone literal transcription it lacks those names.
repros.script:
from tomlkit import comment  # DOC-LITERAL
from tomlkit import document  # DOC-LITERAL
from tomlkit import nl  # DOC-LITERAL
from tomlkit import table  # DOC-LITERAL

doc = document()  # DOC-LITERAL
doc.add(comment("This is a TOML document."))  # DOC-LITERAL
doc.add(nl())  # DOC-LITERAL
doc.add("title", "TOML Example")  # DOC-LITERAL

owner = table()  # DOC-LITERAL
owner.add("name", "Tom Preston-Werner")  # DOC-LITERAL
owner.add("organization", "GitHub")  # DOC-LITERAL
owner.add("bio", "GitHub Cofounder & CEO\nLikes tater tots and beer.")  # DOC-LITERAL
owner.add("dob", datetime(1979, 5, 27, 7, 32, tzinfo=utc))  # DOC-LITERAL
owner["dob"].comment("First class dates? Why not?")  # DOC-LITERAL
